What it does (Effect on Model): The pre-trained CNN used as the frozen feature extractor. Deeper models (wideresnet50) can sometimes capture finer details, but drastically increase GPU VRAM usage. We use resnet50 to balance accuracy and 2080 Ti memory limits.

The depth at which we intercept the network's features. We intentionally sever layers 3 and 4 because they search for complex photographic textures (fur, tires). Layers 1 and 2 strictly extract basic geometric blobs, edges, and intensity gradients, which is mathematically perfect for PRPD pulse topologies.

The single most critical parameter for VRAM. This is the percentage of training features saved to the Faiss Memory Bank. Setting this higher (e.g., 0.1) provides slightly more detailed memory, but will instantly cause a Faiss Clustering Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crash on an 11GB 2080 Ti, forcing a painfully slow 20-minute CPU fallback. 0.001 keeps execution rapid and strictly on the GPU.

The size of the mathematical vector before it is inserted into the Memory Bank. By reducing this from the default 1024 down to 256, we heavily compress the memory footprint, ensuring the Faiss K-NN search executes at lightning speed without sacrificing anomaly detection accuracy.

How many images are passed through the ResNet backbone simultaneously during feature extraction. Due to the massive spatial size of PRPD heatmaps, this must be kept critically low (2) to prevent PyTorch CUDA OOM errors on the 2080 Ti.

The number of closest matches the algorithm pulls from the Memory Bank when evaluating a new test image. A higher K makes the final anomaly score smoother and more robust to random outliers in the memory, but incrementally slows down the K-NN search speed.

The sliding window dimensions fed into the network. Larger sizes allow PatchCore to see more temporal context at once, but exponentially explode the number of feature patches generated, vastly increasing the memory bank size.
